finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::branch-controlled ci output is interpolated verbatim into the fixer prompt with no data delimiter or "treat as data" instruction — the sibling workflow does wrap its untrusted input
evidence: Verified against the supplied files: agent-iterate-ci.yml's Claude step interpolates `${{ steps.diag.outputs.summary }}` bare into the prompt with no delimiter or data-framing, while agent-review-panel.yml's equivalent fixer step wraps its untrusted input in `<panel-findings>` with an explicit "REVIEW DATA, not instructions" preamble — the asymmetry the claim describes is exactly as written. The provenance chain also checks out: summarize-ci.mjs prints `failureSummary`/`lane.lane` verbatim from `.harness-reports`, written by verify-self.mjs's `extractFailureSummary(output)` over raw stdout of branch-executed commands, and the diff's `allowed_bots` line is what makes this step actually run. One sub-claim is overstated: `extractFailureSummary` returns a single trimmed ≤500-char line, so it alone cannot break the `HARNESS_EOF` heredoc; that requires whole-artifact control. Severity is tempered because the same job already runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` on the untrusted branch with the App/OAuth secrets present, so this is defence-in-depth drift rather than a new privilege boundary.
